title: Israel 1970: Institutions under Pressure
status: Design proposal. Not installed. Numerical balance proposals, not historical measurements.

groups.label: The Republic and Its Bargains
groups.subtitle: A parliamentary state with institutions stronger than any one cabinet.

groups.label: Capital from Abroad
groups.subtitle: An unusually powerful funding network, with debt, obligations and exposure.

groups.label: People, Skills and a Place to Live
groups.subtitle: Three paid participation reforms. Added workforce reaches +15% in total.

groups.label: Water, Workshops and the Negev
groups.subtitle: Turn scarce water and practical engineering into national advantages.

groups.label: A Nation in Reserve
groups.subtitle: A sharp army whose mobilisation has a visible civilian bill.

groups.label: An Arsenal beyond the Embargo
groups.subtitle: Repair, adapt and eventually build. Expensive choices with civilian consequences.

groups.label: Connections without a Script
groups.subtitle: Offer cooperation and bargaining positions. Other players retain their decisions.

groups.label: Territory, Settlements and Their Price
groups.subtitle: Separate administration, controlled construction and unilateral foreign footholds.

groups.label: Alignment: the Histadrut State
groups.subtitle: A wage bargain, public enterprises and Sapir's development priorities.

groups.label: Gahal: Ownership and National Resolve
groups.subtitle: Liberal ownership, Herut's social appeal and competing spending priorities.

groups.label: Mafdal: Faith, Service and Land
groups.subtitle: Religious Zionist institutions with separate service and settlement choices.

groups.label: Agudat Israel and Poalei Agudat
groups.subtitle: Communal schooling and welfare, with a separate religious workers' continuation.

groups.label: Independent Liberals: Small Firms, Open Doors
groups.subtitle: Commercial law, tourism and two approaches to foreign-currency risk.

groups.label: HaOlam HaZeh - Koah Hadash
groups.subtitle: A secular parliamentary challenge: scrutiny, civil registration and municipal rights.
groups.gate: HaOlam HaZeh - Koah Hadash is in Power.

groups.label: Rakah: A Jewish-Arab Communist Cabinet
groups.subtitle: A genuine alternative government with a real foreign-policy choice.

groups.label: State List: the Administrative Republic
groups.subtitle: Rafi's dissident continuation: professional management over a party economy.

groups.label: Mapam: the Cooperative Left
groups.subtitle: Inside the Alignment at the start; independent leadership is an alternate political outcome.

groups.label: Maki: Independent Communism
groups.subtitle: A shorter parliamentary continuation, separate from Rakah's Soviet option.

groups.label: Free Center: a Different National Opposition
groups.subtitle: A compact alternative to Gahal, not another generic nationalist tree.

nodes.label: Publish the Coalition Budget
nodes.description: A coalition cannot govern by invoking national necessity for every expenditure. Present the competing claims of defence, housing and civil administration to the Knesset.

nodes.label: A Cabinet across the Aisle
nodes.description: Bringing the principal parliamentary blocs into the cabinet distributes responsibility for security. Every major appropriation will also need a broader political bargain.

nodes.label: A Working Parliamentary Majority
nodes.description: A narrower cabinet can carry a clear legislative programme. Its ability to govern will depend more closely on the demands of its remaining partners.

nodes.label: The Civil Service Commission
nodes.description: An open examination and tender system gives engineers and administrators a career beyond party appointments. The reform takes patronage out of the coalition bargain.

nodes.label: Let the Comptroller Follow the Money
nodes.description: Public enterprises, emergency appropriations and municipal grants will answer to the same audit. Some political allies will find their customary contracts harder to defend.

nodes.label: Renew the Religious Status Quo
nodes.description: A renewed parliamentary understanding protects religious institutions without handing them every question of government. Separate educational commitments receive a defined budget.

nodes.label: Enact the Civil Registration Statute
nodes.description: A common civil register and public-service standard would give the secular state a clearer identity. Religious parties will contest the loss of authority over family and communal affairs.

nodes.label: Equal Access to Municipal Tenders
nodes.description: Development towns and Arab municipalities need functioning roads, utility connections and access to public contracts. Publish allocations instead of distributing them through informal political intermediaries.

effects.label: Selected Israeli Core State: Shared Building Slots

requirements: An owned and controlled Israeli core state with infrastructure capacity.
mechanics: Completion funds one eligible domestic municipal grant with its slot and infrastructure. The state is the eligible owned and controlled Israeli core with the lowest infrastructure, breaking ties by state ID. No target menu or occupied-territory core is assumed.

nodes.label: The Israel Bonds Subscription
nodes.description: A development loan can turn overseas confidence into capital at home. Subscribers receive a state obligation, and the treasury must meet its debt service after the campaign ends.
mechanics: One subscription, one loan. Interest uses the existing MD public-debt economy.

nodes.label: The Overseas Absorption Appeal
nodes.description: Charitable partners can support homes, language courses and civilian services through the absorption institutions. This support is directed at settlement and welfare needs rather than unrestricted military procurement.
mechanics: Completion establishes the restricted 4%-GDP civilian appropriation. Later housing and training focus transactions draw it down against actual costs, never beyond the remaining balance. No unrestricted military cash and no separate spending menu.

nodes.label: The Diamond Bourse Dollar Desk
nodes.description: The diamond trade already connects Israel to international finance. A foreign-currency desk can support specialist exporters, but a smaller range of overseas markets will carry more of the economy.

nodes.label: Jaffa Citrus Export Houses
nodes.description: Packing, refrigeration and marketing can make a familiar export earn more abroad. The resulting income still depends on access to distant customers and their prices.

nodes.label: Turn Subscriptions into Workshops
nodes.description: Borrowed capital must leave productive assets behind. The development tender funds a civilian plant and the power and transport connections needed to keep it operating.

nodes.label: An Export Credit Guarantee Book
nodes.description: A public guarantee lets smaller exporters accept contracts beyond their own balance sheets. The finance ministry must reserve funds against those commitments.

effects.label: Export Guarantee Provision
effects.value: -0.02% of annual GDP per week for 52 weeks

mechanics: Completion directly starts the listed 52-week funded guarantee programme. Its full weekly provision and benefit expire together. No individual guarantee menu.

nodes.label: A Commercial Route through Eilat
nodes.description: A southern route gives commerce another outlet when northern access is uncertain. Building it requires maintenance and dependable arrangements with the countries along the route.
requirements: Israel owns and controls the Negev.

nodes.label: Hold a Foreign-Currency Cushion
nodes.description: Reserving part of the capital inflow reduces the need to borrow during the next import shock. Fewer funds are available for immediate construction.

nodes.label: Let Development Spend the Inflow
nodes.description: Release the reserve into productive construction while the funds are available. The treasury accepts dearer borrowing if the next external shock arrives before the projects mature.

nodes.label: A Long-Term Debt Calendar
nodes.description: Match the repayment calendar to the time required for development assets to earn an income. The treasury exchanges part of its short-term flexibility for more predictable debt service.

nodes.label: An Ulpan with a Job at the End
nodes.description: Language instruction becomes part of an employment service rather than a waiting room. Trained interpreters and placement officers help newcomers use skills they already possess.

nodes.label: Recognise the Engineer and the Nurse
nodes.description: Hospitals and factories cannot afford to leave qualified arrivals in unsuitable work. Professional boards will run conversion courses and practical examinations.

nodes.label: ORT Workshops beyond the Coast
nodes.description: Industrial training in development towns makes skilled employment possible without relocating every household to the coastal cities. Instructors and workshop equipment require a continuing education commitment.

nodes.label: Homes Connected to Work
nodes.description: A housing estate without a road to employment merely moves a shortage elsewhere. Fund the utility links, transport and workshops around the new homes.
requirements: Israel owns and controls the Negev.

nodes.label: Kupat Holim in the Development Towns
nodes.description: Coordinate neighbourhood clinics, referral services and purchasing instead of sending every case to a distant central facility. The health service saves part of its bill while the treasury funds a standing local grant.

nodes.label: Day Care for the Second Shift
nodes.description: Childcare and suitable shift arrangements let more women remain in paid employment. The gain comes from participation, supported by a larger public-service budget.

nodes.label: Hear the Neighbourhood Committees
nodes.description: Give the neighbourhood committees a paid repair programme and a public hearing. Maintenance teams address the homes and services behind the complaints, while the treasury carries the stated appropriation.

history.note: Responds to documented social gaps; it does not force a Black Panthers event or create that later organisation at the 1970 start.

nodes.label: Scholarships across the Social Divide
nodes.description: Merit should not depend on the ability to leave home for years of study. Targeted bursaries and preparatory courses open technical education to households excluded by its incidental costs.

nodes.label: A Skilled Workforce That Stays
nodes.description: Housing, professional recognition and practical training can turn arrival into a lasting career. The objective is a productive civilian economy with room for its citizens, not a limitless supply of reservists.
mechanics: The three participation focuses add exactly +15% workforce together. No party, settlement or military focus adds further workforce. No population is removed from another RP country.

nodes.label: Keep the National Carrier Running
nodes.description: The National Water Carrier is already in service. Pumps, stores and repair crews determine whether its promise reaches the farms at the end of the network.

nodes.label: Hatzerim: More Crop per Drop
nodes.description: A kibbutz workshop can become an exporter of a practical answer to arid farming. Demonstration plots will make the new irrigation method usable beyond its first customers.

nodes.label: Connect the Southern Farms
nodes.description: Distribution lines and roads must reach the same communities. Expanding cultivated land brings higher pumping and maintenance costs with it.
requirements: Israel owns and controls the Negev.

nodes.label: Meter Water before Expanding Acreage
nodes.description: Use the next investment to reduce waste in existing cultivation. Farmers receive a more dependable system, but the ministry postpones its next wave of new districts.

nodes.label: The Reclamation Budget
nodes.description: Water used in the towns need not be lost to every other purpose. A paid treatment and distribution programme broadens the network without pretending that water is unlimited.

nodes.label: New Districts in the Negev
nodes.description: Concentrate the capital on additional cultivated districts. The productive gain arrives with a larger electricity and maintenance bill for the water authority.

nodes.label: Machine Tools from the Kibbutz
nodes.description: Cooperative workshops can manufacture components as well as repair farm equipment. An industrial order book gives rural employment a second source of income.

nodes.label: Offer Ethiopia a Precision-Irrigation Contract
nodes.description: Export the equipment with the knowledge needed to use it. Overseas customers gain a useful system while Israeli suppliers gain a contract rather than an automatic diplomatic alignment.

nodes.label: An Exportable School of Engineering
nodes.description: Universities, agricultural stations and suppliers will share testing facilities. The programme turns specific engineering problems into products without promising the later venture-capital economy overnight.

nodes.label: The Reservist and His Workshop
nodes.description: The same people keep factories working and reserve formations ready. A common register lets the cabinet see what a call-up will cost before issuing it.
mechanics: Exercise and emergency mobilisation are separate national focuses with their complete costs. Neither is activated automatically by the register.

nodes.label: Keep Essential Workshops Open
nodes.description: Reserve assignments can protect the technicians who keep water, repair and power services functioning. Readiness will improve more slowly in units that release those specialists.

nodes.label: Depots before Another Division
nodes.description: A reservist reaches a useful formation only if its stores and transport are ready. Permanent depot staff cost money even when no mobilisation order is issued.

nodes.label: Tal and the Armoured School
nodes.description: Tank crews need maintenance, gunnery and practical exercises more than another ceremonial command. A stronger school also means paying for vehicles, instructors and fuel.

nodes.label: Fortify the Canal Positions
nodes.description: A defended position can save lives, but maintaining a fixed line commits the army to a particular frontier. Construction proceeds only where Israel actually controls the ground.

effects.label: Selected Controlled Sinai Province: Shared Building Slots
Selected Controlled Sinai Province: Land Forts

requirements: Israel controls Sinai and an eligible frontier province with fort capacity.

nodes.label: A Mobile Reserve behind the Front
nodes.description: Keep a formation able to reinforce the threatened sector rather than distribute every unit among static positions. This requires a larger standing transport and personnel establishment.

nodes.label: A College for Lessons Learned
nodes.description: Junior commanders and technicians will be heard alongside the general staff. Turn exercise reports and combat experience into practical training before memory becomes institutional certainty.

nodes.label: Clinics behind the Front
nodes.description: The reserve system leaves families and workplaces exposed to the same emergency. Shelter construction and medical preparation make mobilisation a public responsibility rather than a military abstraction.

nodes.label: A Readiness Calendar the Economy Can Bear
nodes.description: Publish a reserve calendar that the army can train against and civilian employers can plan around. Emergency mobilisation remains available, but cannot become a permanent source of cheap readiness.

effects.label: National Reserve Call-Up Civilian Productivity Penalty

mechanics: Improves the named temporary call-up programme only. No permanent army bonus or extra workforce is added.

nodes.label: Bedek before a New Airframe
nodes.description: Repair and overhaul are the foundation of aviation independence. Expand that capability before committing the country to an aircraft it cannot maintain.

nodes.label: Fund the Nesher Engineering Line
nodes.description: Developing an indigenous fighter requires tooling, test work and imported components. Allocate a real engineering budget rather than treating a national name as a finished aircraft.

effects.label: Nesher Development
effects.value: -0.025% of annual GDP per week for 52 weeks

mechanics: Research and development only. No automatic 1970 fleet and no technology-year bypass.

nodes.label: ELTA: Electronics at the Workbench
nodes.description: Radar and communications suppliers can share a practical testing establishment. Reserving their work for defence makes the military customer less dependent on foreign deliveries.

nodes.label: Give the Arava a Civilian Order Book
nodes.description: A utility aircraft and a business-aviation workshop can earn income outside the defence budget. Civil certification and customer support require attention from the same engineers.

nodes.label: Authorise Tal's Tank Programme
nodes.description: A tank programme begins with repair facilities, comparative trials and a design office. Crew protection is a design objective, and production independence is a long-term commitment.

effects.label: Domestic Tank Development
effects.value: -0.03% of annual GDP per week for 78 weeks

mechanics: Opens the domestic tank development project. It does not grant an operational Merkava at the scenario start.

nodes.label: Gabriel and the Missile Boats
nodes.description: A domestic anti-ship weapon needs vessels, training and reliable maintenance. Naval investment provides another answer to supplier uncertainty without replacing the whole fleet overnight.

nodes.label: Open the Civilian Supplier Catalogue
nodes.description: Civilian firms can use test equipment and subcontracting experience developed for defence. Some of the laboratory schedule will move away from military work.

nodes.label: Give Defence the Test Benches
nodes.description: Concentrate the testing establishment on the urgent military order book. The gain in defence production comes with a smaller civilian share of the engineering effort.

nodes.label: The Technion's First Computing Classes
nodes.description: The new computing faculty can supply engineers to laboratories and industry. A small country must fund its instructors and students before expecting a large research sector.

nodes.label: Offer Uganda an Equipment Contract
nodes.description: Domestic workshops need an order book larger than Israel alone can provide. A foreign customer must agree to an actual equipment sale, its price and delivery schedule.

nodes.description: Diplomats, commercial officers and technical advisers can open doors that military strength cannot keep open by itself. Give their work a permanent establishment.

nodes.description: Technical cooperation can make an embassy useful to its host. An invitation must come from the partner government, and expertise sent abroad still has a budget at home.

nodes.description: Audit the four territorial administrations and give their civilian liaison offices a common standard. Better records ease administration without removing the resistance, supply or personnel costs already present at the start.

nodes.label: Pay for a Civil Administration
nodes.description: A functioning military administration needs records, courts, utilities and paid staff. Better administration can reduce friction while keeping its cost visible to the cabinet.
